newsitem.title: FRANCE: French farm minister offers to pray for rain.
newsitem.headline: French farm minister offers to pray for rain.

text.p: France's agriculture minister on Friday offered a spiritual remedy for farmers facing drought but held back immediate help from public coffers.
Speaking to farmers in the Alpine city of Grenoble, Farm Minister Philippe Vasseur said he was worried by a chronic lack of rain needed to nourish crops at a vital growing stage.
"It is always worrying when you see drought arriving...I am going to end up doing a rain dance in the main square of Grenoble," Vasseur joked at a regional farm show.
Farmers who grow grain, one of France's biggest export earners, are worried that crop yields from this summer's harvest will be damaged after weeks without rain.
Farmers in the north where most wheat is grown have been ordered to stop irrigating their crops for two days a week.
Vasseur pledged to be supportive to farmers but said it was too early to announce any public help.
"Measures will depend on the situation and on the damage caused," he said, adding that underground water resources had not yet dropped to crisis levels.
France has a calamity fund financed partly by the farm industry to compensate farmers for any serious crop damage.
But neither the government nor farmers want to repeat an unpopular "drought tax" that stirred up public hostility to subsidised farmers during a far worse water shortage in 1976.
French forecasters are warning of another bone-dry week with hardly a drop of rain in the next five days.

Weather service Meteo France said on Thursday that rainfall had been as much as 50 percent below normal since January in the north of France and even lower in the south, where some regions had not seen a single drop of rain last month.
But it said it would have to stay dry right through August for a repeat of the drought of 20 years ago.
